budget_items.topic: Year three O&M contract with CTE
budget_items.what_was_said: The final-year operations contract with CTE was described as an increase in the budget, for a stated annual amount starting July 1, 2022. The commission praised CTE as a loyal vendor and voted to approve it.
The fourth quarter bills went out May 19 and the commission voted to accept the commitment amount.
A billing insert told customers about a rate increase taking effect with the next bill; only one customer inquired.

budget_items.topic: FY22 retained earnings and betterment revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: Year-to-date figures show the enterprise back in the black, with back betterment payments from Meadow Woods ahead of plan. A budgeted loss in retained earnings is now projected as a surplus.

budget_items.topic: Future rate increases and Fitchburg/Leominster costs
budget_items.what_was_said: Members noted the coming rate increase would still leave a loss and suggested a fixed small annual increase to cover rising Fitchburg and Leominster charges. Next year was expected to be the worst before leveling off.

budget_items.topic: Upland and White Street betterment estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: Letters to 64 parcels were to go out advertising an engineer's estimate for the combined betterment, with a survey for owners to vote online. Members noted the estimate includes a contingency and material costs are rising.

Fitchburg's monthly invoice, Leominster's quarterly invoice (about 20,000 above the prior quarter and year-ago period, in a wet period) and a record-only counsel invoice were to be paid. The budget had been increased for the Leominster line.
Members said grant and ARPA money may be available to fix inflow and infiltration problems, possibly jointly with Leominster. Staff will research.
A member said plastic septic pipe costs had risen sharply in a year, to justify the betterment as a comparison.

contention.about: Whether the commission should limit sewer use to the sewered portion of a bisected parcel that carries a betterment, and whether owners should be notified.
contention.sides: Members (including one remote) against restricting use of betterment-paying parcels and for deed notice; staff said counsel found the bisection lawful and no deed restriction is required.
contention.words_as_heard: to take something away without letting the homeowner know is not correct i feel it's it's not right

decisions.decision: Town counsel to be asked to meet with the commission on the Chestnut Street bisected-parcel issue; it will go on a future agenda.
The 7-Eleven Mass Ave condo plans will go on the June 14 agenda after the new DPW director reviews them.
The June 14 meeting will be a regular Zoom meeting; the June 28 format will be decided at the next meeting.
Newly elected officers will take effect at the next meeting.

minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission welcomed its new DPW director and reorganized after elections, with the chair, vice chair, and clerk chosen by voice roll call. It discussed the Chestnut Street bisected-parcel problem, approved the CTE year-three contract, the fourth-quarter commitment, and two sets of minutes, and heard a positive FY22 financial update. It settled that the June 14 meeting will be on Zoom.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved the year-three operations contract with CTE, the final year of the contract, starting July 1, 2022.
The commission accepted the fourth-quarter sewer billing commitment; those bills went out May 19.
John Reynolds was elected chair, Brett Ramsey vice chair and Mike Devakis clerk; the new officers take effect at the next meeting.
The business manager reported FY22 year-to-date figures back in the black, with a budgeted retained-earnings loss now projected as a surplus.
Town counsel is to be asked to meet the commission on the Chestnut Street bisected-parcel issue, and the June 14 meeting will be held on Zoom.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills are set by this commission, and members said a coming rate increase would still leave a loss while Fitchburg and Leominster charges rise, so further increases are likely.
A proposed Upland and White Street betterment would put an assessment on 64 parcels, and owners are to be surveyed on it, so affected residents may be asked to vote.
watch_next: June 14 Sewer Commission meeting on Zoom, where the 7-Eleven Mass Ave condo plans are expected after the new DPW director reviews them.
The online owner survey on the Upland and White Street betterment estimate, and a future agenda item with town counsel on Chestnut Street.

Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every officer election, both contract and commitment votes, and the June 14 Zoom decision, with several names and figures garbled by captions. The one substantive difference is the Chestnut Street bisected-parcel item, which ours records as a request to town counsel and the official minutes record as Barb reviewing it with Bill and sending counsel's input. Each record also has items the other lacks.
